failure_reasons.question: What scientific conclusion can the held-out comparison support, after accounting for control complexity and uncertainty? Either a well-supported positive or negative result can satisfy the task; lack of power is not dishonesty.
failure_reasons.reason: The performed comparison is too weak or uncertain to resolve the question at the required level.
failure_reasons.judge_reason: Global DR is well supported (M1-M0 +521.9 [322.0, 728.8]). The required channel and cone tests are not resolved. M2-M1 = -11.1 [-184.6, 102.8], M2 - best M3 = -92.5 [-406.5, 61.8] and C2-M1 = -42.1 [-132.7, 26.6] all have wide CIs that straddle 0. The submission's own post hoc calibration shows real held-out intervals 2.9-8.4x wider than synthetic ones, and the fitted-M2 generator's effect would exceed the real half-width in 0% of cases. So cone-sized effects of the fitted magnitude cannot be excluded. The paper says the cone-vs-control contrast is limited by unmodelled heterogeneity and that the site of DR 'cannot be resolved'. The conclusions are honestly qualified, but the comparison itself is too uncertain to resolve cone-alignment or anisotropy at the required level.
evidence: proposal/logs/synthetic_calibration.json (width ratios; adjusted_power_pos 0.0 for G_M2 M2-M3_opp)
